title: Reading the carbamazepine and abacavir labels

segs.text: Section twenty eight. Carbamazepine and abacavir: one gene, two variants. Carbamazepine, brand name Tegretol, is one of the older antiepileptics still in use. Abacavir, brand name Ziagen, is an antiretroviral for H I V, a nucleoside analogue reverse transcriptase inhibitor. Both carry an H L A B warning, but for a different variant of the same gene, and the hypersensitivity reaction shows up in a different place. She said, The H L A B gene is involved in both, but it's a different genetic variant for carbamazepine compared to abacavir, same gene. Different variants.

Unlike trastuzumab, there is no tumor here. These drugs do not act on a tumor target. The risk comes from H L A alleles the patient inherited, so the patient's own D N A is genotyped. She said, we're not dealing with tumors with these drugs for carbamazepine and abacavir. The variants raise the risk of hypersensitivity. They do not make the drug less effective, and they do not change the dose.

Carbamazepine has two genes to check. The first is H L A B, variant H L A B star fifteen oh two. The second is H L A A, variant H L A A star thirty one oh one, which she said entered the labeling only with the two thousand seventeen revision. Either variant significantly increases the risk of a severe skin reaction: Stevens Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis, S J S or T E N, which can be fatal. The boxed warning says patients with ancestry in genetically at risk populations should be screened for H L A B star fifteen oh two before starting.

Abacavir goes with H L A B star fifty seven oh one. The problem was first seen as massive skin reactions, similar to carbamazepine. The labeling later changed: it is a hypersensitivity reaction involving multiple organs, and the label lists multi organ failure and anaphylaxis among the reactions. So it is not a skin only reaction. The label says to screen all patients for H L A B star fifty seven oh one before starting or restarting abacavir, and the drug is contraindicated in patients who test positive.

The main point is the pairing. She said, They both cause a risk for a hypersensitivity reaction, but carbamazepine is located in the skin, and for abacavir, it's a whole organ hypersensitivity reaction. So one negative H L A B test does not clear both drugs. A patient negative for fifteen oh two may still carry fifty seven oh one. H L A B star fifty eight oh one and H L A D R B one star fifteen oh one belong to neither drug. Those go with allopurinol and amoxicillin clavulanate.
